data.name: Pawan
data.gender_notes: Pawan is used as a male name in hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Sanskrit pavana, 'wind, air', from the root pū, 'to purify'. Its root is Sanskrit pavana (पवन). A classical Sanskrit name for the wind god. Pawan is a Sanskrit name meaning “Wind; air; pure”. Families who choose it generally do so for the quality the name expresses.
data.spiritual_meaning: Pawan expresses “Wind; air; pure”; spiritual readings of the name are interpretive.
data.etymology: From the Sanskrit pavana, 'wind, air', from the root pū, 'to purify'.
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Pawan total 19, reducing to 1. Number 1 is associated with leadership, independence and initiative.

vedic_reference.note: Pawan is a name derived from the Sanskrit language and is associated with Lord Vayu, the Hindu god of the wind. It is mentioned in various Hindu scriptures and is considered a significant name in Hindu mythology.

historical_references.reference: A classical Sanskrit name for the wind god.
